name: IT Technology Risk
description: IT general controls (ITGC) and technology risk management as tested in SOX, SOC 1/SOC 2 and internal audit: governance, assets, access, change, operations, logging, data protection, resilience, third parties and technology lifecycle.
references: COBIT 2019, SOX ITGC / PCAOB AS 2201, NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, CIS Controls v8

categories.name: Governance & Risk Management
categories.objective: Technology risk is identified, owned, measured and governed within the enterprise risk appetite.

items.control: An IT risk management framework and a technology risk appetite with quantified tolerances are approved by the board or risk committee.
items.risk: Technology risk is taken on inconsistently and outside the organisation's appetite.
items.test: Inspect the framework and appetite statement for approver and approval date within the last 12 months, and confirm tolerances are quantified rather than descriptive.
evidence: IT risk management policy with version history and approval page
Board or risk committee minutes recording approval of the technology risk appetite
Appetite statement with numeric tolerances (e.g. Tier 1 downtime hours, unpatched critical count)

items.control: An IT risk register records each risk with an owner, inherent and residual rating, linked controls and treatment plan, and is reviewed quarterly.
items.risk: Known technology risks are untracked, unowned or left untreated.
items.test: For a sample of 10 risks, confirm owner, ratings, linked controls and treatment plan are recorded and that each was reviewed in every quarter of the period.
evidence: Risk register export from the GRC tool (e.g. ServiceNow IRM, Archer) with last-reviewed dates
Quarterly IT risk committee minutes showing register review
Treatment plan status report for High residual risks

items.control: Technology risk roles are defined across the three lines (IT, Risk/Compliance, Internal Audit), with named control owners.
items.risk: Accountability gaps let technology risks fall between teams.
items.test: Inspect the RACI and charters, then interview one control owner per line to confirm they understand their responsibilities.
evidence: Technology risk RACI naming accountable roles
Approved charters for the IT risk committee and Internal Audit
Control owner list from the GRC tool
items.other: COBIT APO01; IIA Three Lines Model

items.control: Technology key risk indicators are reported to senior management monthly against defined thresholds.
items.risk: Deteriorating technology risk is not visible until it causes an incident.
items.test: Inspect three monthly KRI packs; confirm thresholds are defined, breaches are flagged and each breach has an owner and action.
evidence: Monthly KRI dashboard (e.g. patch SLA attainment, Tier 1 availability, overdue audit issues, EOL asset count)
Distribution email to the CIO and risk committee
Action log for threshold breaches

items.control: Policy exceptions and risk acceptances are risk-assessed, approved at the authority level matching residual risk, and expire within 12 months.
items.risk: Policy deviations persist indefinitely without anyone formally accepting the risk.
items.test: For a sample of exceptions, confirm a risk assessment, approval at the correct authority, compensating controls and an unexpired end date.
evidence: Exception register with approver, compensating control and expiry date
Signed risk acceptance forms for sampled exceptions
Report of expired exceptions and their follow-up

items.control: Internal Audit covers IT under a risk-based plan, and findings are tracked until closure is independently validated.
items.risk: Control weaknesses go undetected or audit findings are never fixed.
items.test: Inspect the IT audit plan for risk-based coverage; for a sample of closed findings, confirm closure was validated with evidence.
evidence: Risk-based IT audit plan approved by the audit committee
Issue tracker with owner, due date, status and validation evidence
Ageing report of overdue audit issues

categories.name: Asset & Configuration Management
categories.objective: Technology assets are known, owned, securely configured and disposed of safely.

items.control: The hardware inventory (CMDB) records owner, location and criticality and is reconciled to automated discovery monthly.
items.risk: Unknown devices are not patched, monitored or protected.
items.test: Compare a current discovery scan to the CMDB, investigate assets found in only one source, and confirm the reconciliation ran each month.
evidence: CMDB extract with owner, location, criticality and last-seen date
Monthly CMDB-to-discovery reconciliation (e.g. ServiceNow Discovery, Lansweeper)
Tickets resolving unmatched assets

items.control: A software and SaaS inventory records version, licence count and business owner, including SaaS found through SSO and expense data.
items.risk: Shadow IT and unlicensed software process company data without oversight.
items.test: Compare the inventory to the SSO app catalogue and three months of expense or card data for SaaS not on the list.
evidence: Software inventory report with version, licences and owner
SaaS discovery report from SSO logs or a SaaS management tool
Approved software list

items.control: Applications are tiered by business criticality and Tier 1 dependencies (infrastructure, interfaces, vendors) are mapped.
items.risk: Protection and recovery effort is not focused on the systems that matter most.
items.test: Inspect tiering criteria and results; for each Tier 1 application confirm a dependency map updated within 12 months.
evidence: Application criticality tiering with business owner sign-off
Dependency maps for Tier 1 services
Cross-reference of tiering to BIA results

items.control: Hardened configuration baselines exist for servers, endpoints, databases and network devices, and configuration drift is scanned continuously.
items.risk: Insecure default settings leave systems open to compromise.
items.test: Inspect baseline standards; obtain the latest compliance scan and confirm failing settings are ticketed or covered by an approved exception.
evidence: Hardening standards mapped to CIS Benchmarks per platform
Configuration compliance scan (e.g. Qualys Policy Compliance, Defender for Cloud, AWS Config)
Drift remediation tickets

items.control: Storage media are sanitised or destroyed before disposal or reuse, with certificates retained per serial number.
items.risk: Data is recovered from retired, resold or lost equipment.
items.test: Select a sample of disposed assets from the CMDB and trace each serial number to a certificate of destruction or sanitisation record.
evidence: CMDB disposal log for the period
ITAD vendor certificates of destruction listing serial numbers
Leaver asset-return checklist

categories.name: Access Control
categories.objective: Access to applications, databases and infrastructure is authorised, appropriate and promptly removed.

items.control: New and changed access is requested through a ticket and approved by the system or data owner before it is granted.
items.risk: Users obtain access the system owner never authorised.
items.test: From the population of access grants, select 25 and confirm owner approval is timestamped before the grant and access matches the request.
evidence: System-generated population of access grants for the period
Sampled access tickets showing approver and approval timestamp
Role catalogue mapping job roles to entitlements

items.control: Leaver access is disabled within one business day of termination (same day for privileged users), reconciled to the HR leaver report.
items.risk: Former staff or contractors retain access and misuse it.
items.test: For 25 leavers from the HR termination report, compare termination date to disable dates in the directory, IdP and in-scope applications.
evidence: HR termination report for the audit period
Directory and IdP deactivation logs (e.g. Active Directory, Okta, Entra ID)
Leaver reconciliation showing days to disable per system

items.control: User access reviews run quarterly for privileged access and semi-annually for standard access to in-scope systems, and removals are actioned.
items.risk: Inappropriate access accumulates through role changes and is never removed.
items.test: For sampled reviews, confirm the user list was complete and system-generated, the reviewer was independent, sign-off was dated, and removals were completed.
evidence: Review packs with evidence the user list was complete and accurate (query and row count)
Reviewer sign-off with date
Tickets showing removals completed within SLA

items.control: Privileged accounts are named, justified, vaulted and session-logged across directory, database, cloud and network layers.
items.risk: Admin accounts are misused or compromised with no accountability.
items.test: Obtain privileged group and role memberships at each layer; confirm each account is individually assigned, justified and managed in the PAM vault.
evidence: Privileged account inventory with owner and justification
PAM vault configuration and checkout logs (e.g. CyberArk, BeyondTrust)
Membership exports of Domain Admins, DBA roles and cloud admin roles

items.control: MFA is enforced for remote access, cloud consoles and all privileged access, and the password policy meets the corporate standard.
items.risk: Stolen passwords give attackers remote, cloud or admin access.
items.test: Inspect IdP policies to confirm MFA scope, review every exclusion for justification, and compare the MFA enrollment report to active users.
evidence: Conditional access or sign-on policy export showing MFA enforcement and exclusions
MFA enrollment report compared to active user list
Password policy settings screenshot

items.control: Segregation-of-duties rules prevent developers deploying their own code and block incompatible ERP roles, and conflicts are monitored.
items.risk: One person can make and approve a change or transaction, enabling fraud or error.
items.test: Inspect the SoD rule set, obtain the current conflict report and confirm each conflict is removed or covered by a documented mitigating control.
evidence: SoD rule set (e.g. developer vs deployer, create vendor vs pay vendor)
SoD conflict report from the ERP or GRC tool
Mitigating control evidence for accepted conflicts

items.control: Service accounts are inventoried with an owner, cannot log on interactively, and have credentials rotated within policy.
items.risk: Unowned service accounts with static passwords are used for lateral movement.
items.test: Obtain the service account list and confirm each has an owner, interactive logon denied and last password change within the rotation period.
evidence: Service account inventory with owner and purpose
Vault rotation report or pwdLastSet extract
Group policy denying interactive logon

categories.name: Change Management
categories.objective: Changes to production systems are authorised, tested, independently approved and traceable.

items.control: Every production change, whether standard, normal or emergency, is recorded in the ITSM tool under a documented change policy.
items.risk: Untracked changes cause outages or introduce unauthorised functionality.
items.test: Obtain the change population and confirm it is complete by comparing it to deployment tool logs for in-scope systems.
evidence: Change management policy defining change types and approvals
Complete change population for the period from ITSM (e.g. ServiceNow, Jira Service Management)
Standard change catalogue with pre-approval records

items.control: Changes are tested, with results attached to the change record, before approval for production.
items.risk: Defective changes reach production and corrupt data or break services.
items.test: For 25 sampled changes, inspect attached test evidence and confirm testing completed before approval.
evidence: Sampled change tickets with attached UAT or QA results
CI pipeline test reports linked to the change
Business UAT sign-off emails or approvals

items.control: An authorised approver independent of the developer approves each change before deployment.
items.risk: Changes are deployed without independent authorisation.
items.test: For the same sample, confirm the approver is on the authorised list, differs from the developer, and approved before the deployment timestamp.
evidence: CAB minutes or approval records
Approval vs deployment timestamps from ITSM and CI/CD tools
Authorised approver list

items.control: Emergency changes are approved retrospectively within two business days and reviewed for misuse of the emergency route.
items.risk: The emergency process is used to bypass normal change control.
items.test: Select emergency changes from the period, confirm retrospective approval within the window, and check the emergency share of total changes for trends.
evidence: Emergency change report for the period
Retrospective approval timestamps
Monthly emergency change trend reviewed by the Change Manager

items.control: Production deployments are reconciled to approved change tickets weekly to detect unauthorised changes.
items.risk: Out-of-process changes go undetected.
items.test: Inspect the reconciliation for a sample of weeks and confirm every unmatched deployment was investigated and resolved.
evidence: Deployment log to change ticket reconciliation
File integrity monitoring alerts on production servers
Investigation records for unmatched deployments

items.control: Development, test and production are separated, developers have no production write access, and production data is masked before use in non-production environments.
items.risk: Developers alter production directly, or production data is exposed in test.
items.test: Inspect production access group membership for developers, and inspect masking job logs for the most recent production-to-test refresh.
evidence: Environment architecture diagram
Production access group membership export
Data masking procedure and job logs

categories.name: IT Operations
categories.objective: Systems run reliably, failures are resolved and vulnerabilities are patched on time.

items.control: Critical batch jobs and interfaces are monitored, and failures automatically raise tickets that are resolved and rerun.
items.risk: Failed jobs leave financial or operational data incomplete or late.
items.test: Inspect scheduler alert configuration and, for a sample of failures, confirm a ticket was raised and the job was rerun successfully.
evidence: Job scheduler failure report (e.g. Control-M, Airflow, Autosys)
Alert routing configuration
Incident tickets with rerun confirmation
items.other: COBIT DSS01; SOX ITGC computer operations

items.control: IT incidents are classified by severity against SLAs, and P1/P2 incidents receive a root cause analysis with tracked actions.
items.risk: Outages recur because root causes are not fixed.
items.test: For a sample of P1/P2 incidents, confirm severity, SLA adherence, a completed RCA and closure of its actions.
evidence: Incident report with severity and SLA metrics
Major incident RCA reports
Problem records linked to incidents with action status

items.control: OS and application patches are deployed within severity-based SLAs (e.g. critical in 14 days, high in 30 days).
items.risk: Known vulnerabilities remain exploitable.
items.test: Obtain patch compliance by severity and tier for three months, confirm SLA attainment, and check that out-of-SLA systems have approved exceptions.
evidence: Patch compliance report by severity and asset tier (e.g. Intune, SCCM, Ansible)
Patch SLA standard
Approved exceptions with compensating controls

items.control: Compute, storage and network capacity is forecast and reviewed quarterly, with actions for resources nearing thresholds.
items.risk: Resource exhaustion causes outages or degraded service.
items.test: Inspect two quarterly capacity reviews and confirm forecasts and actions exist for resources above 80% utilisation.
evidence: Capacity trend reports for compute, storage and network
Capacity review meeting minutes
Scaling or procurement tickets

categories.name: Monitoring & Logging
categories.objective: Availability issues and suspicious activity on critical systems are detected and can be reconstructed.

items.control: Tier 1 services have availability and performance alerting with 24x7 on-call cover and defined escalation.
items.risk: Outages go undetected until customers report them.
items.test: Inspect alert rules for each Tier 1 service and the on-call rota, and trace a recent alert from trigger to acknowledgement.
evidence: Alert rules with thresholds (e.g. Datadog, Prometheus, SCOM)
On-call rota and escalation policy (e.g. PagerDuty, Opsgenie)
Alert-to-acknowledge time report for the period

items.control: Logs from Tier 1 systems are centralised in a SIEM, with time synchronised to a trusted source.
items.risk: Activity on critical systems cannot be reconstructed after an incident.
items.test: Compare the SIEM source list to the Tier 1 asset list, investigate gaps, and inspect NTP configuration on a sample of servers.
evidence: SIEM log source inventory compared to the Tier 1 asset list
Log ingestion health dashboard
NTP configuration from sampled servers

items.control: Privileged activity on in-scope systems (admin logons, group changes, audit log clearing) is reviewed weekly.
items.risk: Misuse of admin access goes unnoticed.
items.test: Inspect a sample of weekly reviews, confirm the report logic is complete, and confirm anomalies were investigated.
evidence: Privileged activity report with query logic
Reviewer sign-off per week
Investigation tickets for anomalies

items.control: Logs are retained for at least 12 months and protected from modification by the administrators being logged.
items.risk: Attackers or insiders delete or alter logs to cover their tracks.
items.test: Inspect log storage permissions and immutability settings, and confirm the oldest retrievable record meets the retention period.
evidence: Log storage access permissions
Immutability or WORM configuration
Query showing oldest retained event date

categories.name: Data Protection & Backup
categories.objective: Business data is classified, encrypted and recoverable.

items.control: Data is classified, and systems holding confidential or regulated data are identified in the CMDB.
items.risk: Sensitive data is stored in places nobody knows to protect.
items.test: Inspect the classification scheme and confirm that a sample of systems known to hold personal or financial data are tagged in the CMDB.
evidence: Data classification policy
CMDB report of systems tagged by data classification
Data discovery scan results (e.g. Microsoft Purview, BigID)

items.control: Confidential data is encrypted at rest (databases, storage, laptops) and in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher).
items.risk: Data is exposed when storage, devices or network traffic are compromised.
items.test: Inspect encryption settings for sampled databases and storage, the laptop encryption compliance report, and a TLS scan of external endpoints.
evidence: Database and storage encryption settings (e.g. TDE, KMS-managed keys)
Laptop disk encryption compliance report
External TLS scan results

items.control: Backups of in-scope systems run automatically per the backup policy, and failures are alerted and remediated.
items.risk: Data cannot be recovered because backups silently failed.
items.test: Compare the backup job list to in-scope systems, then inspect job results for a sample of days and remediation of failures.
evidence: Backup policy with scope, frequency and retention
Backup job configuration compared to the in-scope system list (e.g. Veeam, Commvault, AWS Backup)
Failure alerts and remediation tickets

items.control: Restores of Tier 1 systems are tested at least annually, and restore times are compared to the RTO.
items.risk: Backups exist but cannot be restored in time.
items.test: Inspect restore test records for each Tier 1 system and compare actual restore time to the RTO.
evidence: Restore test records with date, system and outcome
Actual vs target RTO comparison
Issues raised from failed or slow restores

items.control: At least one backup copy is immutable or offline and cannot be deleted with production administrator credentials.
items.risk: Ransomware or a compromised admin destroys backups along with production.
items.test: Inspect immutability settings and the access model for the backup copy, and confirm production admins cannot delete it.
evidence: Object lock or immutability configuration
Backup architecture diagram showing the isolated copy
Access permissions for the backup vault

categories.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
categories.objective: Critical technology services can be restored within business-approved recovery objectives.

items.control: A business impact analysis sets maximum tolerable downtime, RTO and RPO for critical processes and is reviewed annually.
items.risk: Recovery capabilities do not match what the business actually needs.
items.test: Inspect the BIA for review date and business sign-off, and confirm RTO and RPO values flow into the DR plan.
evidence: BIA with business owner sign-off
RTO and RPO by application tier
Cross-reference of BIA to DR plan

items.control: A disaster recovery plan for Tier 1 systems is failover-tested annually, and test findings are tracked to closure.
items.risk: Recovery fails in a real disaster because the plan was never proven.
items.test: Inspect the DR test report for scope, RTO and RPO achieved and findings, then confirm findings are closed or tracked.
evidence: DR plan with runbooks per Tier 1 system
DR test report with RTO and RPO achieved
Findings tracker from the DR test

items.control: Single points of failure are identified in architecture reviews, and Tier 1 infrastructure has redundancy (HA clusters, multiple availability zones).
items.risk: A single component failure takes down a critical service.
items.test: Inspect the architecture review and confirm Tier 1 services are deployed redundantly, or that the single point of failure has an accepted risk.
evidence: Architecture resilience review
HA or multi-zone deployment configuration
Risk acceptances for remaining single points of failure

categories.name: Third-Party Risk
categories.objective: Technology suppliers and cloud services are selected, contracted and monitored in line with their risk.

items.control: Technology vendors are inventoried and tiered by criticality, data access and substitutability.
items.risk: Critical or high-risk vendors are not identified for proper oversight.
items.test: Compare the vendor register to accounts payable vendor master data and confirm tiering criteria were applied to a sample.
evidence: Vendor register with tier, data access and owner
Tiering questionnaire and criteria
Reconciliation of the register to accounts payable vendor list

items.control: Critical vendors complete security and resilience due diligence (questionnaire, SOC 2 Type II, financial health) before contract signature.
items.risk: Vendors with weak controls are onboarded with access to systems or data.
items.test: For vendors onboarded in the period, confirm due diligence was completed and approved before the contract start date.
evidence: Completed security questionnaires (e.g. SIG Lite, CAIQ)
SOC 2 Type II report review memo noting exceptions
Due diligence approval dated before contract start

items.control: Vendor contracts include security requirements, right to audit, SLAs, breach notification within a set number of hours, and exit assistance.
items.risk: The organisation lacks contractual leverage when a vendor fails or is breached.
items.test: For a sample of critical vendor contracts, check for each required clause against the standard contract checklist.
evidence: Contract clause checklist
Executed MSA, DPA and security schedule
Legal review notes for deviations

items.control: Critical vendors are monitored annually: SLA performance, refreshed SOC reports, and mapping of complementary user entity controls (CUECs) to internal controls.
items.risk: Vendor control failures or service degradation go unnoticed.
items.test: For sampled critical vendors, inspect the latest SOC report review, its bridge letter and the CUEC mapping, plus SLA reports.
evidence: Annual SOC report review with bridge letter
CUEC-to-internal-control mapping
Quarterly SLA performance reports

items.control: Cloud shared-responsibility boundaries are documented, and exit plans and concentration risk are assessed for critical cloud providers.
items.risk: Customer-side cloud responsibilities are missed, or the organisation is locked into a failing provider.
items.test: Inspect the shared responsibility matrix and exit plan for each critical provider, and confirm concentration risk was assessed.
evidence: Shared responsibility matrix per cloud provider
Documented exit plans
Provider concentration analysis

categories.name: Technology Lifecycle & SDLC
categories.objective: Technology stays supportable, and new systems and migrations are delivered with risk controls built in.

items.control: End-of-life and end-of-support technology is identified, with a funded remediation roadmap or compensating controls.
items.risk: Unsupported systems accumulate unpatchable vulnerabilities.
items.test: Compare the EOL register to vendor lifecycle dates for a sample of platforms, and confirm each EOL asset has a dated plan or exception.
evidence: EOL and EOS register from the CMDB
Approved upgrade roadmap with funding
Exceptions with compensating controls such as isolation

items.control: In-house development follows a secure SDLC with mandatory peer review and automated SAST and dependency scanning in CI.
items.risk: Vulnerable or malicious code reaches production.
items.test: Inspect branch protection settings and, for sampled merges, confirm an independent reviewer and passing security scans.
evidence: Branch protection rules requiring review (e.g. GitHub, GitLab)
Pull requests showing approver other than author
SAST and SCA results from the pipeline

items.control: Security and technology risk requirements are assessed at project initiation and at each stage gate.
items.risk: Projects go live with unassessed risks or missing controls.
items.test: For projects delivered in the period, confirm a risk assessment and security sign-off exist at the design and go-live gates.
evidence: Project risk assessment
Stage gate approvals with security sign-off
Go-live readiness checklist

items.control: Data migrations reconcile record counts and financial control totals between source and target, and the business signs off before cutover.
items.risk: Data is lost or corrupted during migration to a new system.
items.test: Inspect migration reconciliations for record counts and hash or control totals, confirm differences were explained, and confirm sign-off before cutover.
evidence: Source-to-target reconciliation report
Explanation of reconciling differences
Business cutover sign-off

items.control: Key end-user computing tools (spreadsheets and low-code apps used for financial or regulatory output) are inventoried with version, access and review controls.
items.risk: Errors in uncontrolled spreadsheets flow into financial or regulatory reporting.
items.test: Inspect the EUC inventory and, for sampled high-risk EUCs, confirm restricted access, version history and an independent review of logic.
evidence: EUC inventory with risk rating
Access permissions on the EUC storage location
Documented logic review for high-risk EUCs
